newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil barges, cargoes idle as buyers fade.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil barges, cargoes idle as buyers fade.

text.p: Lack of buying interest pushed NWE gas oil further into the doldrums on Wednesday and traders said aggressive offers kept downward pressure on most premiums.
"It's a pure disaster," said one barge trader who sought in vain to sell. "It was so quiet I thought it was a Friday."
Benchmark Jan futures finished $2.75 down at $219.25 a tonne, pulled lower by NYMEX heating oil in languid paper trade.
On the barge market sellers outnumbered buyers, offering parcels of 0.2 percent refinery grade heating oil at around Jan IPE -$1/1.25, with buying interest notionally around Jan IPE +$1.50.
Small parcels traded at Jan IPE -$1 early but interest later faded.
Storage grade low sulphur diesel was offered at around Jan IPE +9 and refinery grade at around Jan IPE +$10/11.
In cargoes, a small Russian 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil with -15 cold filter plugging point traded at Jan IPE +$3.75 loading December 20-24 into Germany, slightly firmer.
French grade heating oil was a touch lower at Jan +$4.50/5.50. Low sulphur diesel was Jan IPE +$14.50/15.50.
